note: How-to recipes for Clay and HubSpot. Add or fix one any time: keep steps short, one action each. Menus move: when a step no longer matches the screen, update it and change 'checked'.

recipes.title: Find local businesses and their websites
recipes.keywords: find leads companies businesses local google maps search list build table
steps: Open Clay and create a new workbook, then add a table.
Choose to find companies or local businesses (the Google Maps style source) as the starting source.
Enter the business type and the city or area, then set the number of results.
Run it and check the rows: name, website, phone and address.
Delete obvious chains and rows without a website before enriching (saves credits).
tips: Clay Free has a row cap: pull small, clean batches.
Our own $0 alternative: HQ Tools lead finder (dse.py find) for the same job.

recipes.title: Enrich a list with emails and socials (waterfall)
recipes.keywords: enrich email emails find contact waterfall social instagram linkedin owner
steps: Open the table with your companies (it needs a website or domain column).
Add an enrichment column and pick a work-email or contact finder.
Map the input to the domain column, then add more providers in order to make a waterfall (it stops at the first hit).
Run on 5 rows first to check quality and credit cost, then run on the rest.
Add a column that validates the email before you use it.
tips: Run on a few rows before the whole table: credits go fast.
Our free waterfall for websites: gtm.py enrich.

recipes.title: Write a personalised first line with AI
recipes.keywords: ai personalise personalize opener first line message claygent prompt write copy
steps: Add an AI column (the 'use AI' or Claygent option).
Write the prompt with column references, e.g. the company name, city and one fact you found.
Ask for one short sentence and forbid made-up facts.
Run on 5 rows, read every output, and tighten the prompt.
Only then run on the full table.
tips: Keep openers permission-based: offer to send what you found, never free work.
Never use the em dash in copy (house rule).

recipes.title: Score and filter leads
recipes.keywords: score scoring filter qualify priority hot warm cold formula
steps: Add a formula column that adds points for what matters (e.g. no reviews widget, few reviews).
Add a filter on the table view to show only rows above your cut-off.
Save that filtered view so you can reuse it.
Export or send only the filtered view.

recipes.title: Export a table to a CSV for HQ or the CRM
recipes.keywords: export csv download send list cockpit crm import out
steps: Open the table (or the filtered view you want).
Use the table menu to export or download as CSV.
Save it, then in Citadel use BPS → CRM → Import CSV, or put it in the engine's send-lists folder for the cockpit.
tips: Name columns business, city, website, email, instagram, facebook so our importers map them automatically.

recipes.title: Import a CSV into Clay
recipes.keywords: import upload csv bring in add rows from file
steps: Create a new table and choose to import from CSV.
Upload the file and check each column's type.
Run your enrichment columns on the new rows.

recipes.title: Import contacts or companies from a CSV
recipes.keywords: import contacts companies csv upload list add bulk
steps: In HubSpot, open Contacts (or Companies).
Click Import, then start an import from a file on your computer.
Choose one file, one object (contacts or companies).
Map each CSV column to a HubSpot property; create a property for anything missing.
Review and finish, then open the import summary to fix any errors.
tips: Include the email column for contacts so HubSpot de-duplicates.

recipes.title: Set up a deal pipeline with stages
recipes.keywords: pipeline deals stages sales board setup
steps: Open Settings, then Objects, then Deals, then Pipelines.
Edit the default pipeline or create one.
Name the stages in order (e.g. Contacted, Replied, Call booked, Proposal sent, Won, Lost).
Save, then open Sales, then Deals, to see the board.
tips: Match the stages to the Citadel CRM so both read the same.

recipes.title: Create a deal from a contact and move it
recipes.keywords: deal create move stage contact board won lost
steps: Open the contact record.
In the Deals card on the right, create a deal and choose pipeline and stage.
On the deals board, drag the deal to the next stage as things move.
Mark it Won or Lost when it ends, with a short reason.

recipes.title: Create a list (segment) of contacts
recipes.keywords: list segment filter group contacts view saved
steps: Open Contacts, then Lists (sometimes called Segments).
Create a list and choose active (updates itself) or static.
Add filters, e.g. Lifecycle stage is Lead and City is Tampa.
Save and use it for follow-ups or reports.

recipes.title: Log a call, email or note on a contact
recipes.keywords: log call note email activity record timeline
steps: Open the contact.
Use the Note, Call or Log activity buttons at the top of the timeline.
Write the outcome and the next step, and set a follow-up task with a date.
tips: Logging is record-keeping only: you still send every message yourself.

recipes.title: Create a private app key (for scripts later)
recipes.keywords: api key token private app integration connect script
steps: Open Settings, then Integrations, then Private Apps (or Legacy apps on newer accounts).
Create an app, give it only the scopes you need (e.g. contacts and deals read/write).
Copy the token straight into the PC settings file the tool names: never paste it into a chat.

recipes.title: The whole GTM system, start to finish
recipes.keywords: gtm system overview plan outbound process stack start end high level strategy
steps: Pick one market and one offer (who, what problem, what result).
Build the list: Sales Navigator or Apollo for B2B people, Clay for companies and enrichment, HQ lead finder for local businesses.
Enrich and verify: emails (waterfall in Clay or Apollo), then verify before any send.
Write the message: one gap you found, a permission question, no free work.
Send from warmed inboxes in Instantly (email) and by hand on LinkedIn; keep daily caps.
Automate the boring parts in n8n: replies into the CRM, alerts, follow-up tasks.
Track in HubSpot or the Citadel CRM: replied, call booked, won, lost.
Review weekly with the outcomes report and change one thing at a time.
tips: Stack for GTM Engineering in DBI: Claude Code, Clay, n8n and a CRM are required; add Sales Navigator, Apollo, Instantly or Lemlist by market.

recipes.title: Build a lead list in Sales Navigator
recipes.keywords: sales navigator salesnav linkedin lead list search filters saved search accounts people
steps: Open Sales Navigator, then Lead filters (people) or Account filters (companies).
Set the core filters: geography, industry, company headcount, job title or function, seniority.
Add buying signals: changed jobs recently, posted recently, or growing headcount.
Save the search so new matches show up, and save good leads to a Lead list.
Work the list by hand: view profile, connect with a short note, follow up after acceptance.
tips: Don't scrape or auto-click LinkedIn: it breaks their terms and risks your account.
Keep connection requests low and personal on a new account.

recipes.title: Use Sales Navigator signals for timing
recipes.keywords: signals alerts changed job posted hiring timing trigger warm
steps: Open your saved searches and lists and check the alerts feed.
Prioritise people who changed job, posted, or whose company is hiring for your area.
Mention the signal in one line of your first note, then your permission question.

recipes.title: Find contacts and verified emails in Apollo
recipes.keywords: apollo find contacts people emails search export verified list
steps: Open Apollo, then Search, then People.
Filter by job title, location, company size and industry; add 'email verified' if offered.
Save the people you want to a list.
Export the list to CSV (watch your export credits), or push to your CRM if connected.
Check emails again before sending if they are old.
tips: The free plan has monthly credit limits: export only what you will contact.

recipes.title: Enrich an existing CSV in Apollo
recipes.keywords: apollo enrich upload csv match fill missing
steps: Open the enrichment or data import area and upload your CSV.
Map columns (name, company, domain) and run the match.
Download the enriched file and remove rows without a verified email.

recipes.title: Set up Instantly sending inboxes and warm-up
recipes.keywords: instantly setup inbox inboxes warmup warm up domain dns email account sending
steps: Buy separate sending domains (never your main one) and set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
Connect each inbox in Instantly (Email accounts, then Add new).
Turn on warm-up for every inbox and wait about 2 to 3 weeks before campaigns.
Keep each inbox to a modest daily send limit.
tips: Purchases are yours to make: $0 mode applies until a client pays.

recipes.title: Launch an Instantly campaign from a CSV
recipes.keywords: instantly campaign launch sequence upload leads csv steps schedule send
steps: Create a campaign and upload the leads CSV (map email, first name, company and your personal line).
Write the sequence: step 1 plus 1 to 2 follow-ups a few days apart; use the variables.
Set the schedule (their time zone, weekdays) and daily limits.
Choose the sending inboxes, turn on stop-on-reply, then launch.
Check replies daily and move interested ones to your CRM.
tips: You press launch yourself: agents only prepare the CSV and copy.

recipes.title: Read Instantly results and fix a campaign
recipes.keywords: instantly analytics results open reply bounce rate fix deliverability
steps: Open the campaign analytics: sent, opened, replied, bounced.
If bounces are high, verify the list again and pause bad inboxes.
If replies are low, change one thing (subject, first line or offer) and test again.

recipes.title: Build a simple n8n workflow
recipes.keywords: n8n workflow build automation trigger node webhook schedule start
steps: Open n8n and create a new workflow.
Add a trigger: Schedule, Webhook, or an app trigger (e.g. new email).
Add the action nodes in order (e.g. read data, transform, write to CRM).
Click Execute workflow to test with real data and check each node's output.
Save and turn the workflow on (Active).
tips: Our local n8n runs at C:/Users/Administrator/n8n-local.

recipes.title: Send replies from email into the CRM with n8n
recipes.keywords: n8n reply router replies crm hubspot email classify route
steps: Trigger on new emails in the sending inbox (or an Instantly webhook for replies).
Add a node that sorts the reply (interested, not now, unsubscribe).
For interested replies, create or update the contact and deal in HubSpot.
Send yourself an alert (email or Slack) with the next step.
Test with a few sample replies before turning it on.
tips: Our tested version: the Reply Router in engine-c-upwork/item3-reply-router.

recipes.title: Run a multichannel sequence in Lemlist
recipes.keywords: lemlist sequence multichannel linkedin email campaign
steps: Create a campaign and import leads.
Build steps: email, then a manual LinkedIn task, then a follow-up email.
Set delays and sending limits, connect your inbox, then launch yourself.

recipes.title: Set up review requests in GoHighLevel
recipes.keywords: gohighlevel ghl review request reputation google reviews automation sms smb
steps: Create the client's sub-account and connect their Google Business Profile under Reputation.
Add the review link and customise the review-request message.
Build a workflow: trigger on job done (tag, form or pipeline stage), then send the review request by SMS and email.
Add one reminder after 2 to 3 days if no review.
Test with your own number before switching it on.
tips: Reviews are the SMB opening offer; other systems come after.

recipes.title: Missed-call text-back in GoHighLevel
recipes.keywords: gohighlevel ghl missed call text back sms phone smb inquiry
steps: Buy or port the client's number in the sub-account (their purchase).
Create a workflow triggered by a missed call.
Send an instant SMS: thanks for calling, how can we help, plus a booking link.
Notify the owner and test by calling and hanging up.

recipes.title: Prepare and run a high-ticket sales call
recipes.keywords: ascent sales call closing prep high ticket zoom calendly objection close script
steps: Read the lead's application or form answers and note their goal, pain and budget.
Open the offer's call script and the objection notes.
Run the call: rapport, discovery, gap, offer, objections, close.
Log the outcome straight after (closed, follow-up, lost) with the reason.
Send the payment or contract link the offer owner gave you.
tips: Score yourself after each call with the Ascent scorecard.

recipes.title: Find high-ticket offers that hire closers
recipes.keywords: ascent find offers closers remote commission job boards
steps: Search closer job boards and communities for remote commission roles.
Check the offer: price, lead flow, commission %, and reviews of the founder.
Apply with a short message plus your recorded practice call.
tips: Never pay to get a closer role.

recipes.title: Build an abandoned cart flow in Klaviyo
recipes.keywords: klaviyo abandoned cart flow email sms checkout started shopify revenue recovery
steps: Connect the store (Shopify integration) in Klaviyo.
Create a flow from the Abandoned Cart template (trigger: Checkout Started).
Set timing: email 1 after about 1 hour, email 2 after 1 day, optional SMS.
Add the dynamic cart block and a clear button back to the cart.
Exclude people who ordered, test with a real checkout, then turn it live.
tips: Show the client the recovered revenue in the monthly report.

recipes.title: Build a welcome series in Klaviyo
recipes.keywords: klaviyo welcome series signup popup list subscribe flow
steps: Create a sign-up form (popup) with a welcome offer and connect it to a list.
Create a flow triggered by joining that list.
Write 3 emails: welcome plus offer, brand story, best sellers.
Test the form and the flow, then turn them on.

recipes.title: Edit a podcast episode in Descript
recipes.keywords: descript podcast edit episode audio remove filler words clean export
steps: Import the recording; Descript makes a transcript.
Remove filler words and long pauses from the transcript.
Use Studio Sound to clean the audio, then add intro and outro.
Export the audio (MP3) and the video if recorded.
tips: Practise on your own practice episodes first, never free work for a real host.

recipes.title: Make short clips from an episode in CapCut
recipes.keywords: capcut clips shorts reels captions vertical podcast
steps: Pick 3 to 5 strong 30 to 60 second moments from the episode.
Import the video in CapCut and set the canvas to 9:16.
Add auto captions and check the spelling.
Add the show name and a hook at the top, then export.

recipes.title: Write and schedule a LinkedIn ghostwritten post
recipes.keywords: authority linkedin ghostwriting post hook write schedule client voice
steps: Collect the client's raw ideas (voice note, call notes).
Write a strong first line, one idea, short paragraphs, one clear ending.
Get the client's approval, then schedule it in LinkedIn's own scheduler.
Track likes, comments and profile views weekly.
tips: Build your portfolio on a made-up persona first.

recipes.title: Build an AI receptionist in Vapi
recipes.keywords: vapi voice ai receptionist assistant phone number calls booking cal.com
steps: Create an assistant in Vapi: business name, hours, services and FAQs in the prompt.
Choose a natural voice and test it in the browser.
Connect a phone number and set the client's missed calls to forward to it.
Connect booking (Cal.com) so callers can book.
Send call summaries to the owner via n8n.
tips: Mystery-call the business first to show the gap.

recipes.title: Connect Cal.com booking to the AI receptionist
recipes.keywords: cal.com cal booking calendar availability voice ai
steps: Create the event type (length, buffers, hours) in Cal.com.
Copy the booking link or API details into the assistant's booking tool.
Test a booking end to end and check the calendar invite.

recipes.title: Automate client intake with n8n
recipes.keywords: automation n8n intake form documents pdf email reply onboarding ai automation
steps: Map the client's current intake: form, email, documents.
Trigger on a new form submission (webhook or form node).
Send an instant reply with next steps and a booking link.
Save the details and files to their CRM or drive.
Notify the team; test with sample submissions, then go live.
tips: Price: build $500-$8,000 plus monthly care from $150.
